title: Pivot tables: fields, values, filters and grouping

videos.script: Every question so far has needed a formula. A total by channel. A total by month. A total by product and channel. {{formulas}} A pivot table asks all of those questions at once, and you write none of the formulas. You drag a field. {{drag}} Channel goes into rows. Revenue goes into values. Three totals and a grand total appear, and they match the formulas of lesson five, to the last real. {{match}} Drag product down the side and channel across the top, and it becomes a grid. Drag customer into the filter, and the grid shows one customer at a time. {{areas}} A sum can become a count, an average, or a share of the total. Dates can be grouped into quarters. And a year that looked like a collapse turns out to be half a year. {{group}} There is one catch. A pivot table reads a copy of the data. Change a sale, and the pivot does not notice until you refresh it. {{refresh}} So this lesson builds your first pivot tables on the Sales table, and checks every number against a formula you already trust.
